title: ColorRef: Calibrating Verbal Feedback for Color Revision
abstract: arXiv:2611.25653v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: People rarely specify an exact color when asking someone to revise a design: they might say \textit{a little darker} or \textit{more blue} after seeing a proposal. A language-model assistant must then infer not only which way to change the color, but how far. We study this distinction with \textsc{ColorRef}, a color reference game in which a model guesses a color from a description and a teacher, knowing a recorded target hidden from the guesser, supplies verbal corrections. On 1{,}000 crowd-sourced description--target pairs, three rounds of deterministic oracle feedback reduce mean target distance from 42.33 to 22.15 $\Delta E_{76}$. However, those corrections provide additional information, and improvement alone does not establish well-calibrated feedback following. A controlled Qwen3-14B diagnostic reveals a more specific failure: following a requested direction and ordering graded phrases do not guarantee a suitable step size; strong

translated_title: ColorRef：为颜色修订校准言语反馈
translated_abstract: 人们在请他人修改设计时很少指定确切的颜色：在看到方案后，他们可能会说“稍微暗一点”或“更蓝一点”。此时，语言模型助手不仅需要推断颜色应该朝哪个方向改变，还要推断改变的幅度有多大。我们通过 ColorRef 来研究这一区别——这是一个颜色指代游戏，模型根据描述猜测颜色，而一位知晓（对猜测者隐藏的）记录目标的教师提供言语纠正。在 1,000 个众包的描述-目标对上，三轮确定性神谕反馈将平均目标距离从 42.33 ΔE76 降低到 22.15 ΔE76。然而，这些纠正提供了额外信息，仅凭改进本身并不能证明模型能够良好地遵循经过校准的反馈。一项受控的 Qwen3-14B 诊断实验揭示了一个更具体的失败：遵循所要求的方向并对分级用语进行排序，并不能保证合适的步长；强力……
tldr: 该论文提出颜色指代游戏 ColorRef，揭示语言模型虽然能正确理解颜色修改的方向和分级用语，却无法据此产生幅度合适的颜色调整步长。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces ColorRef, a color reference game showing that language models can follow the direction and graded wording of verbal feedback but fail to take a suitably calibrated step size when revising colors.
